spans.text: (The person saying Kaddish proclaims our hope that) soon, in our lifetime, the entire world, which Hashem created precisely according to His Will, will recognize Hashem as the Source of all and will see the sanctity, perfection, and purpose of all He has done.

אָמֵן. יְהֵא שְׁמֵהּ רַבָּא מְבָרַךְ לְעָלַם וּלְעָלְמַיָּא—(We all enthusiastically respond:) Absolutely correct! May everyone (including me!), everywhere, and forever, see that all His actions are great and deserving of praise!

יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיִשְׁתַּבַּח—(The person saying Kaddish then points out that) in reality, the true greatness and power of Hashem far exceeds any praises that we mere humans could say. And to that we respond: אָמֵן—Absolutely correct!

אֵל אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם—(As we take out the Torah, we proclaim that) we know that we have not fulfilled everything that it says in Your Torah, but please, in Your lovingkindness, do not rebuke us. Instead, forgive us, and help us see Your Presence in the world.
—When the Aron traveled (leading Bnei Yisrael through the desert);
וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה, קוּמָה יְהֹוָה וְיָפֻצוּ אֹיְבֶיךָ וְיָנֻסוּ מְשַׂנְאֶיךָ מִפָּנֶיךָ—Moshe requested that all our enemies and those who hate us should run away in fright!

כִּי מִצִּיּוֹן תֵּצֵא תוֹרָה, וּדְבַר יְהֹוָה מִירוּשָׁלָיִם—(So too, when the Beis Hamikdash will be rebuilt, all the nations of the world will come to Yerushalayim to learn the truth and will proclaim:) "Torah comes out of Zion (to light up the entire world) and Hashem's truth comes (only) from Yerushalayim!"

בָּרוּךְ שֶׁנָּתַן תּוֹרָה לְעַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ—We thank You, Hashem, for giving us Your Torah and trusting us with the responsibility (now—even before Mashiach comes) to spread its truth everywhere (by our actions and words).

בְּרִיךְ שְׁמֵהּ דְּמָרֵא עָלְמָא—Hashem, You are the Source of everything! Please redeem us, rebuild the Beis Hamikdash, shine Your light on us, and accept all our tefillos. May we all live long and happy lives. Protect me, all that is mine, and all that belongs to all of Bnei Yisrael. You feed all, You sustain all, You rule over all—and I am Your servant, who bows before Your glorious Torah! I do not put my trust in humans or in angels, but rather, I place my complete trust in You, for You are the One True God, Whose Torah and Prophets are all true, and Whose actions are all good and true! Please, open my heart to Your Torah! And fulfill all that I and all Your nation Yisrael wish for—but only if what we wish for is really good for us and will give us life and peace!
(Holding the Sefer Torah, the chazzan calls out:) Declare the greatness of Hashem with me; —גַּדְּלוּ לַיהוָה אִתִּי and together we will praise Him! —וּנְרוֹמְמָה שְׁמוֹ יַחְדָּו

(And we respond:) —לְךָ יְהוָה הַגְּדֻלָּה Any power, victories, or glory that we have been granted are really all Yours, because everything is really Yours! The kingship and rule of leaders (here on earth) derive from You! Therefore, we praise You and bow ourselves before You.
—אַב הָרַחֲמִים Our merciful Father, have mercy on us, help us in fulfilling our mission and protect us from the yetzer hara, and fulfill our requests so we may dedicate ourselves to serving You.

(When calling up the first aliyah—the gabbai proclaims:) May the sovereignty of Hashem over us as His special nation be revealed to all soon, and may Hashem show loving-kindness to us. Everyone should praise Hashem and show honor to His Torah, but specifically, let (name, son of father's name) come forward. We all thank You, Hashem, for giving Your Torah to Bnei Yisrael.

(And everyone declares together: As Moshe told the Jews who had resisted the temptation to worship the idol Baal-Pe'or) and all of you who stood firm and remained close with Hashem; —חַיִּים כֻּלְּכֶם הַיּוֹם you are all alive today (you merit Divine protection in this life, you merit eternal life, and you live lives of meaning that make a lasting impression on the world).

בָּרְכוּ אֶת יְהוָֹה הַמְּבֹרָךְ—(The one receiving the aliyah calls out to us:) We must make the world realize (by how we speak and how we conduct ourselves daily) that Hashem is the Source of all, and that everything He does is perfect and for the ultimate best.

בָּרוּךְ יְהוָֹה הַמְּבֹרָךְ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד—(and we respond:) Yes, we pledge to make the world realize (by how we speak and how we conduct ourselves daily) that Hashem is the Source of all, and that everything He does is perfect and for the ultimate best, for all eternity!

בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָֹה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; מֶלֶךְ—You take care of us; אֱלֹהֵינוּ—and You rule the entire הָעוֹלָם; אֲשֶׁר בָּנוּ מִכָּל הָעַמִּים (we are so happy that) You have chosen us, Bnei Yisrael, out of all the nations
of the world; וְנָתַן לָנוּ אֶת תּוֹרָתוֹ—and given us Your Torah. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָֹה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; נוֹתֵן הַתּוֹרָה—Who gives (us) the Torah.

בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָֹה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; מֶלֶךְ—You take care of us; אֱלֹהֵינוּ—and You rule the entire הָעוֹלָם; אֲשֶׁר נָתַן לָנוּ תּוֹרַת אֱמֶת (we are so happy that) You have given us the Torah of truth; וְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם נָטַע בְּתוֹכֵנוּ—and implanted eternal life within us. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָֹה—You,
Hashem, are the Source of everything; נוֹתֵן הַתּוֹרָה—Who gives (us) the Torah.

בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; אֱלֹהֵינוּ—You take care of us; מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם—and You rule the entire world; הַגּוֹמֵל לְחַיָּבִים—You, Who grant good to the undeserving; שֶׁגְּמָלַנִי כָּל טוֹב—has given much good to me!
(and we respond:) מִי שֶׁגְּמָלְךָ כָּל טוֹב—May He Who granted you much good; הוּא יִגְמָלְךָ כָּל טוֹב סֶלָה—He should continue to grant you much good, forever.

יִתְגַּדַּל וְיִתְקַדַּשׁ שְׁמֵהּ רַבָּא—(The person saying Kaddish proclaims our hope that) soon, in our lifetime, the entire world, which Hashem created precisely according to His Will, will recognize Hashem as the Source of all and will see the sanctity, perfection, and purpose of all He has done.

אָמֵן. יְהֵא שְׁמֵהּ רַבָּא מְבָרַךְ לְעָלַם וּלְעָלְמֵי עָלְמַיָּא—(We all enthusiastically respond:) Absolutely correct! May everyone (including me!), everywhere, and forever, see that all His actions are great and deserving of praise!

יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיִשְׁתַּבַּח—(The person saying Kaddish then points out that) in reality, the true greatness and power of Hashem far exceeds any praises that we mere humans could say. And to that we respond: אָמֵן—Absolutely correct!
וְזֹאת הַתּוֹרָה—This is the very same Torah that was given to us by Moshe at the command of Hashem.

עֵץ חַיִּים הִיא—The Torah is a tree of life for those who attach themselves to it, and those who uphold it are happy. Its ways are pleasant and bring peace, and it ensures eternal life and a happy and meaningful life; indeed, the Torah is vast and magnificent.
יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶי אָבִינוּ—May it be the will of our Father in Heaven:

• To rebuild the Beis Hamikdash, and may we feel His Presence among us, Amen!
• To have mercy on us and keep all plagues and destruction far away from us, Amen!
• To take care of all our Torah leaders, their families, and all their students, Amen!
• To give us good news of the arrival of Mashiach and the ingathering of all Jews, Amen!
And אַחֵינוּ כָּל בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל—all our fellow Jews; הַנְּתוּנִים—who are בַּצָּרָה וּבַשִּׁבְיָה—in any kind of distress, trouble, or danger; הָעוֹמְדִים—

please, הַמָּקוֹם יְרַחֵם עֲלֵיהֶם—wherever they are; בֵּין בַּיָּם וּבֵין בַּיַּבָּשָׁה—Hashem, have mercy on them; וְיוֹצִיאֵם מִצָּרָה לִרְוָחָה—get them out of their difficulties; וּמֵאֲפֵלָה לְאוֹרָה—and take them from the darkness to the light; וּמִשִּׁעְבּוּד לִגְאֻלָּה—and from oppression to freedom; וְנֹאמַר הַשְׁתָּא בַּעֲגָלָא וּבִזְמַן קָרִיב—immediately! אָמֵן—Amen!
(Holding the Sefer Torah, the chazzan calls out:) May the whole world recognize the Presence of Hashem, and praise Him for all that He does!
(And we respond:) (Everyone should realize that) the majesty of Hashem is far beyond the earth and the Heaven; and that we, Bnei Yisrael, are His chosen nation and have always remained close to Him.

לְדָוִד מִזְמוֹר—The entire earth belongs to Hashem. Therefore, who will succeed here and be worthy of blessings? Only those who are sincere in the service of Hashem, who use this material world for noble and non-selfish goals and who deal with others with honesty and integrity! We hope for the day when all of civilization will recognize Hashem and live by these values.

וּבְנֻחֹה יֹאמַר—We hope for the day that the real Aron Kodesh will be placed in the Beis Hamikdash and the Kohanim will do the avodah! Please, bring Mashiach soon! The Torah is the perfect "instruction for life." עֵץ חַיִּים הִיא—It is a tree of life for those who attach themselves to it, and those who uphold it are happy. Its ways are pleasant and bring peace. Hashem, please help us return to You and Your Torah!

As we pointed out earlier, Ashrei follows the aleph-beis. The significance is that in all areas of our life (aleph to tav), we need Hashem and His help, we are supported by Him, and His providence is constant. As we transition out of tefillah into our regular school day/workday, it is crucial to keep this in mind.

Out there in the "real world," it can be difficult sticking to our values, and many times we find ourselves in uncomfortable situations. Therefore, we want to stress to ourselves that "אַשְׁרֵי יוֹשְׁבֵי בֵיתֶךָ"—Happy are those who, wherever they are, are living in the house of Hashem (i.e., are living a meaningful and spiritually growing life), and that true happiness comes from not compromising our principles under social pressure.

In Pesukei D'Zimrah, the phrase "פּוֹתֵחַ אֶת יָדֶךָ" is understood as a statement praising Hashem: He opens His Hand and gives everyone what they need. Here, as we transition out of tefillah into our workday, it is understood as a request: Please, Hashem, open Your Hand and give us what we need!

As we transition to our everyday activities, we must focus on the last line of "וִיבָרֵךְ כָּל בָּשָׂר שֵׁם קָדְשׁוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד"—Everyone (will be so impacted by my words and actions, that they too) will bless Hashem," and we must be sure to conduct ourselves in such a manner wherever we are and whatever we do.

אַשְׁרֵי יוֹשְׁבֵי בֵיתֶךָ—Happy are those who (wherever they are) are living in the house of Hashem (are living a meaningful and spiritually growing life); עוֹד יְהַלְלוּךָ סֶּלָה—they will constantly praise You (since they see all the circumstances of their life as opportunities for growth). אַשְׁרֵי

הָעָם שֶׁכָּכָה לּוֹ—Happy and fortunate are we, the nation (Bnei Yisrael) that has all this (glorious history and great mission); אַשְׁרֵי הָעָם שֶׁיהוָֹה אֱלֹהָיו—happy and fortunate are we, the nation (Bnei Yisrael) that has Hashem as our personal God Who takes care of us.

תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד—A song of praise by David HaMelech (תהילים קמה):
אֲרוֹמִמְךָ אֱלוֹהַי הַמֶּלֶךְ—I will exalt and revere You (since I realize that the essence of Hashem as my personal God and Ruler of the entire universe is way beyond our human comprehension); וַאֲבָרְכָה שִׁמְךָ—and (at the same time) I thank You (in the following verses) for all that You have done and will do (for me personally and for our nation); לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד—since the beginning of time and until the end of days.

בְּכָל יוֹם אֲבָרְכֶךָּ—You are the Source of everything that happens to me each and every day, and I thank You for it all (even though some of those things are hard to understand); וַאֲהַלְלָה שִׁמְךָ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד—and in the end of days, I will truly praise You (as all becomes clear).

גָּדוֹל יְהוָה וּמְהֻלָּל מְאֹד—As much as we will thank and praise Hashem, and proclaim Hashem is "great" and is "extremely praised"; וְלִגְדֻלָּתוֹ אֵין חֵקֶר—(the truth is that) the greatness of Hashem is beyond our real comprehension ("the more you know, the more you realize that you don't know").
דּוֹר—Each generation will praise Your actions to the next generation; וּגְבוּרֹתֶיךָ יַגִּידוּ—and will tell them of Your (miraculous) mighty deeds (that they experienced).
הֲדַר כְּבוֹד הוֹדֶךָ—I will discuss (with everyone) the beauty of Your natural world; וְדִבְרֵי נִפְלְאוֹתֶיךָ אָשִׂיחָה—as well as speak of Your wonders (which are beyond our comprehension).

וֶעֱזוּז נוֹרְאֹתֶיךָ יֹאמֵרוּ—Says David HaMelech:) Others (are impressed by and) speak of Your miraculous wonders; וּגְדוּלָּתְךָ אֲסַפְּרֶנָּה—but I speak of Your constant chessed and daily greatness (which is no less miraculous)!

זֵכֶר—They (one generation passing down the heritage to the next) will speak of Your abundant goodness (notwithstanding whatever difficulties that generation may have endured); וְצִדְקָתְךָ יְרַנֵּנוּ—and they sing about Your generosity (that Hashem blesses us with more than the strict letter of the law would dictate).

חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם יְהֹוָה—Hashem is gracious (giving us goodness more than we deserve) and merciful; (and that is apparent in the fact that He is) אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם וּגְדָל חָסֶד—slow to anger, and thus shows His true greatness through His abundant chessed.

טוֹב יְהֹוָה לַכֹּל—Hashem is good to all (of humanity—even those who have not yet lived up to their potential); וְרַחֲמָיו עַל כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו—and His mercy extends to all that He has created (even the smallest of the animal world).

יוֹדוּךָ יְהֹוָה כָּל מַעֲשֶׂיךָ—All of Your creations will thank You (for Your goodness); וַחֲסִידֶיךָ יְבָרְכוּכָה—but Your righteous ones (who have used their God-given gifts to increase sanctity and goodness into the world) will draw increased energy from You, the Source of all blessing, and in turn (by their good deeds) they will increase blessing in Your world.

כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתְךָ יֹאמֵרוּ—They (Your righteous ones) will discuss the glory of Your Kingdom (the Hand of Hashem as seen in the beauty and complexity of the natural world—which we take for granted, and therefore must be discussed a lot); וּגְבוּרָתְךָ יְדַבֵּרוּ—and they will also tell of Your mighty open miracles (which are clear and do not need much discussion).

לְהוֹדִיעַ לִבְנֵי הָאָדָם גְּבוּרֹתָיו—But when they speak to the common man, first they tell about Hashem's might and open miracles (since that is easy for people to see); וּכְבוֹד הֲדַר מַלְכוּתוֹ—and (from the open miracles they) then explain to the common people how to see the Hand of Hashem in the daily miracles of "nature."

מַלְכוּתְךָ מַלְכוּת כָּל עֹלָמִים—Your Kingship is over all the "worlds" (the multitude of spiritual spheres and worlds that are beyond our comprehension); and וּמֶמְשַׁלְתְּךָ בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר—Your Rulership spans eternity and governs each unique generation (in its own special role in Your master plan, all of which is also beyond our human comprehension).

(Though Hashem is "busy" ruling over the entire universe and eternity, yet still He looks after each and every one of us constantly, and) He supports every individual who has fallen (spiritually or emotionally); וְזוֹקֵף לְכָל הַכְּפוּפִים—and He helps every person who is bent over (from his struggles) to get up (and continue his climb toward personal perfection).

(Therefore) every creature, from the smallest to the greatest, looks to You with hope (that You will take care of them); וְאַתָּה נוֹתֵן לָהֶם אֶת אָכְלָם בְּעִתּוֹ—and You do give each one its (physical, spiritual, and emotional) sustenance—just at the time they really need it.

(Thus we ask of You) Please open Your Hand; פּוֹתֵחַ אֶת יָדֶךָ—and give each person רָצוֹן what they need in order to be satisfied. (If you feel you are not getting what you need—focus on the next verse…)

All—צַדִּיק יְהוָֹה בְּכָל דְּרָכָיו that Hashem does is just and righteous (even though as humans it does not always appear that way to us); וְחָסִיד בְּכָל מַעֲשָׂיו—and He applies that justice with great kindness.

(In)—קָרוֹב יְהוָֹה לְכָל קֹרְאָיו truth,) Hashem is close to all who call to Him; לְכֹל but one—אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָאֻהוּ בֶּאֱמֶת must call out to Hashem with emes—honesty and sincerity. (This means that (1) you do not say one thing in your tefillos but then by your actions distance yourself from Hashem; (2) in general, whenever you speak it is with honesty, i.e., you are a "man of your word" and sincere; and (3) it is clear from your actions that you are sincere in your requests from Hashem, since you are doing whatever you personally can do to achieve those goals.)
—He fulfills the will of those who fear Him; רְצוֹן יְרֵאָיו יַעֲשֶׂה—and He hears their cries (in times of trouble) and He saves them. (That is for those who serve Hashem from fear [מיראה].)
(But) those who serve Hashem from love (מאהבה), He will protect them from troubles in the first place!

(Alternatively,) for those who serve Hashem from love (מאהבה), He reserves and preserves (שומר) their ultimate and eternal reward to be given in Olam Haba; וְאֵת כָּל הָרְשָׁעִים יַשְׁמִיד—and Hashem will destroy all evil.

May my mouth declare the praises of Hashem (so powerfully and sincerely, that); וִיבָרֵךְ—everyone—כָּל בָּשָׂר שֵׁם קָדְשׁוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד (will be so impacted by my words and actions, that they too) will bless Hashem and see Him as the Source for all blessings—for eternity!

(And to sum up that entire Chapter 145 in one sentence:) וַאֲנַחְנוּ נְבָרֵךְ יָהּ—And each of us (in our way, based on our own life experiences,) will thank Hashem and see Him as the Source of blessing in our individual lives; מֵעַתָּה וְעַד עוֹלָם—now and forever (no matter what will happen! To sum it all up in one word:); הַלְלוּיָהּ—whatever happens, praise Hashem!

—Please, Hashem, answer us in times of trouble and distress; accept our tefillos and grant us what we ask for. May we shout for joy at Your salvation! Some trust their chariots and their horses (their own physical power), but we call to Hashem
and put our trust in Him. יְהוָה הוֹשִׁיעָה —Please, Hashem, save us, answer us when we call to You.

"Mashiach will come to Zion and to those of Bnei Yisrael who have not defected from their faith," says Hashem. "My bris with Bnei Yisrael is eternal, and the words of Torah will never cease from you, your children, and all your descendants, forever!" promises Hashem.

—We realize that You, Hashem, are completely beyond our comprehension, yet we sing Your praises just as the angels in Heaven proclaim: קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ —The sanctity of Hashem can be felt in ALL worlds, from the very highest world of angels down to the very lowest world, our material world; מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ —His Presence can be felt everywhere. And as the Serafim (the highest levels of angels) proclaim: בָּרוּךְ כְּבוֹד יְהוָה —The essence of Hashem is completely beyond us (even the highest angels); it is מִמְּקוֹמוֹ —from His place (up there, it all makes sense)!

יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֲבוֹתֵינוּ —(As we go out and face the world we ask:) Hashem Who took care of the Avos, please direct our hearts to Your service, and have mercy on us when we make mistakes, for You, Hashem, are forgiving, and are kind to all who
call to You. Shower us with Your blessings; save us from difficulties. Happy is the person who places their trust in You!

—בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֱלֹהֵינוּ שֶׁבְּרָאָנוּ לִכְבוֹדוֹ Thank You for creating us as Your unique nation and giving us a Torah of truth. Open our hearts to Your Torah and inspire us to do the right things! And may we live to see the coming of Mashiach.

—בָּרוּךְ הַגֶּבֶר אֲשֶׁר יִבְטַח Blessed is the person who truly trusts in Hashem and is secure in his belief that all Hashem does is for his best (even if it is hard to see). Hashem never abandons those who seek Him.

(The chazzan proclaims our hope that) soon, in our lifetime, the entire world, which Hashem created precisely according to His Will, will recognize Hashem as the Source of all and will see the sanctity, perfection, and purpose of all He has done.

Instant Insight: The first four requests we make from Hashem all begin with the phrase יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶי—May it be the will of our Father in Heaven," but the last one, "אַחֵינוּ כָּל בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל" does not. Why? Because when we view all fellow Jews as "אַחֵינוּ"—all members of one big family, and there is unity among us—that itself ensures that Hashem will answer our tefillos.
יְהַלְלוּ / הוֹדוּ / לְדָוִד מִזְמוֹר / וּבְנֻחֹה יֹאמַר
As the Torah is being placed in the aron kodesh, we say:

blocks.en: Why are we saying this again?

spans.text:
Instant Insight:
There is no נ in Ashrei—why? The Maharal says that these pesukim, starting with the letters of the aleph-beis, express the inherent meaning (based on Kabbalah) of those letters. The inherent meaning of נ is נפילה—a falling. Here David HaMelech is describing what Hashem does, and Hashem does not cause our fallings! Our mistakes are the result of our own poor choices! In the next verse we are told what Hashem does in regard to our fallings—סוֹמֵךְ יְהוָֹה לְכָל He helps us הַנֹּפְלִים—get back up!

Crucial Instant Insight:
It does not say that Hashem is close to all קראוהו who—באמת now call to Him with honesty and integrity. Rather, אשר יקראוהו who will—באמת call to Him with honesty, in the future tense. This means that if right now you have a very "up and down" relationship with Hashem, and you struggle with being 100 percent sincere, 100 percent of the time, and at times you are a bit of a hypocrite as far as what you promise Hashem and what you end up doing—still, as long as you are committed to being your—יקראוהו באמת goal is to be completely sincere, honest, and genuine in your relationship with Hashem—then already now He will listen to Your requests for help to get there!
אלו ימים שאין אומרים בהם למנצח: ר"ח, חוה"מ, אסרו חג, תשעה באב, חנוכה, שני ימי פורים קטן וגדול, ערב פסח וערב יום הכפורים, גם אין אומרים אותו בבית האבל ר"ל
אין אומרים פסוק ואני זאת בריתי בבית האבל ובתשעה באב:
